agencies.name: AbilityOne Commission
agencies.description: The AbilityOne Commission creates job opportunities for people who are blind or have other significant disabilities in the manufacture and delivery of products and services to the Federal Government.

agencies.name: Access Board
agencies.description: The Access Board is an independent federal agency devoted to accessibility for people with disabilities. The Board develops and maintains design criteria for the built environment, transit vehicles, telecommunications equipment, and for electronic and information technology.

agencies.name: Administration for Children and Families        (ACF)
agencies.description: The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) funds state, territory, local, and tribal organizations to provide family assistance (welfare), child support, child care, Head Start, child welfare, and other programs relating to children and families.

agencies.name: Administration for Native Americans        (ANA)
agencies.description: The Administration for Native Americans (ANA) promotes self-sufficiency and cultural preservation for Native Americans by providing social and economic development opportunities through financial assistance, training, and technical assistance.

agencies.name: Administrative Conference of the United States        (ACUS)
agencies.description: The Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) is an independent federal agency dedicated to improving federal agency administrative processes and procedures.

agencies.name: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
agencies.description: The Administrative Office of the United States Courts handles the nonjudicial, administrative business of the United States Courts such as maintaining statistics and managing Court budgets.

agencies.name: Advisory Council on Historic Preservation        (ACHP)
agencies.description: The Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) encourages the preservation of historic properties across the nation.

agencies.name: Agency for Global Media
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media, formerly known as the Broadcasting Board of Governors, broadcasts news and information about the United States and the world to audiences abroad.

agencies.name: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality        (AHRQ)
agencies.description: The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) supports research to improve the quality, safety, efficiency, and effectiveness of health care for all Americans.

agencies.name: Agency for International Development        (USAID)
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) is the principal U.S. agency to extend assistance to countries recovering from disaster, trying to escape poverty, and engaging in democratic reforms.

agencies.name: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR)
agencies.description: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) responds to, and protects people from harmful chemical exposures.

agencies.name: Agriculture Department        (USDA)
agencies.description: The Department of Agriculture (USDA) provides leadership on food, agriculture, natural resources, and related issues.

agencies.name: Air Force Reserve
agencies.description: The Air Force Reserve Command performs missions and supports Air Force operations.

agencies.name: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau        (TTB)
agencies.description: The Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) collects taxes and enforces regulations on alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and ammunition.

agencies.name: Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Bureau        (ATF)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) enforces federal criminal laws regulating the firearms and explosives industries.

agencies.name: AmeriCorps
agencies.description: Formerly known as the Corporation for National and Community Service, AmeriCorps, and AmeriCorps Seniors engage volunteers in serving directly with nonprofit organizations to tackle the nation's most pressing challenges.

agencies.name: AmeriCorps Seniors
agencies.description: AmeriCorps Seniors is a network of volunteer programs for Americans 55 years and older. Volunteers work in their community doing academic tutoring and mentoring, elderly care, disaster relief, and more.

agencies.name: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service        (APHIS)
agencies.description: The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) protects and promotes U.S. agricultural health, regulates genetically engineered organisms, administers the Animal Welfare Act, and manages wildlife damage.

agencies.name: Antitrust Division
agencies.description: The Antitrust Division promotes economic competition through enforcing and providing guidance on antitrust laws and principles.

agencies.name: Archives, National Archives and Records Administration        (NARA)
agencies.description: The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) preserves U.S. government records, manages the Presidential Libraries system, and publishes laws, regulations, Presidential, and other public documents.

agencies.name: Arctic Research Commission        (USARC)
agencies.description: The U.S. Arctic Research Commission (USARC) develops and recommends a national Arctic research policy.

agencies.name: Bankruptcy Courts
agencies.description: Each of the 94 federal judicial districts  handles bankruptcy matters, and in almost all districts, bankruptcy cases are filed in the bankruptcy court. Bankruptcy laws help people who can no longer pay their creditors get a fresh start by liquidating their assets to pay their debts, or by creating a repayment plan.

agencies.name: Barry M. Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation
agencies.description: The Barry Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation awards scholarships to college students who intend to pursue careers in science, mathematics, and engineering.

agencies.name: Botanic Garden
agencies.description: The Botanic Garden is a living plant museum that educates visitors about the importance of plants to the well-being of humans, and to Earth’s fragile ecosystems.

agencies.name: Bureau of Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade        (TTB)
agencies.description: The Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) collects taxes and enforces regulations on alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and ammunition.

agencies.name: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives        (ATF)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) enforces federal criminal laws regulating the firearms and explosives industries.

agencies.name: Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection        (CFPB)
agencies.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) helps consumers by providing educational materials and accepting complaints. It supervises banks, lenders, and large non-bank entities, such as credit reporting agencies and debt collection companies. The Bureau also works to make credit card, mortgage, and other loan disclosures clearer, so consumers can understand their rights and responsibilities.

agencies.name: Bureau of Engraving and Printing        (BEP)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) produces United States currency notes, operates as the nation's central bank, and serves to ensure that adequate amounts of currency and coin are in circulation.

agencies.name: Bureau of Indian Affairs        (BIA)
agencies.description: The mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) is to enhance the quality of life, to promote economic opportunity, and to carry out the responsibility to protect and improve the trust assets of American Indians, Indian tribes, and Alaska Natives.

agencies.name: Bureau of International Labor Affairs        (ILAB)
agencies.description: The Bureau of International Labor Affairs (ILAB) works to improve working conditions, raise living standards, protect workers’ ability to exercise their rights, and address the workplace exploitation of children and other vulnerable populations.

agencies.name: Bureau of Land Management        (BLM)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) manages outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production on public lands.

agencies.name: Bureau of Ocean Energy Management        (BOEM)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) promotes energy independence, environmental protection, and economic development by managing offshore energy resources.

agencies.name: Bureau of Reclamation
agencies.description: The Bureau of Reclamation is a provider of wholesale water and hydroelectric power in the U.S.

agencies.name: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement        (BSEE)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) provides oversight and enforcement to promote safety, protect the environment, and conserve offshore resources.

agencies.name: Bureau of the Fiscal Service
agencies.description: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service manages all federal payments and collections, and provides government-wide accounting and reporting services. You can contact them to buy bonds or to check on the maturity of bonds you own.

agencies.name: Capitol Police
agencies.description: U.S. Capitol Police Officers work to protect life and property, investigate criminal acts, and enforce traffic regulations on U.S. Capitol Grounds. Officers are also responsible for protecting members, officers of Congress, and their families.

agencies.name: Career, Technical, and Adult Education, Office of        (OCTAE)
agencies.description: The Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education (OCTAE) administers and coordinates programs that are related to adult education and literacy, career and technical education, and community colleges.

agencies.name: Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion        (CNPP)
agencies.description: The Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion (CNPP) works to improve the health and well-being of Americans by developing and promoting dietary guidance that links scientific research to the nutrition needs of consumers.

agencies.name: Center for Parent Information and Resources        (CPIR)
agencies.description: The Center for Parent Information and Resources (CPIR) offers information for children and young people with disabilities under 22 years of age.

agencies.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention        (CDC)
agencies.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) collaborates to create the expertise, information, and tools that people and communities need to protect their health through health promotion, prevention of disease, injury and disability, and preparedness for new health threats.

agencies.name: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services        (CMS)
agencies.description: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) provides health coverage to more than 100 million people through Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, and the Health Insurance Marketplace. The CMS seeks to strengthen and modernize the Nation’s health care system, to provide access to high quality care and improved health at lower costs.

agencies.name: Chemical Safety Board        (CSB)
agencies.description: The Chemical Safety Board (CSB) investigates industrial chemical accidents.

agencies.name: Chief Acquisition Officers Council        (CAOC)
agencies.description: The Chief Acquisition Officers Council (CAOC) monitors and improves the federal acquisition system.

agencies.name: Chief Financial Officers Council        (CFO)
agencies.description: The Chief Financial Officers Council (CFO) works to improve financial management in the U.S. government.

agencies.name: Chief Information Officers Council
agencies.description: The CIO Council is the principal interagency forum on Federal agency practices for information technology management.

agencies.name: Child Support Enforcement, Office of        (OCSS)
agencies.description: The Office of Child Support Services (OCSS) assures that support (both financial and medical) is available to children through locating parents, establishing paternity, identifying support obligations, and enforcing those obligations.

agencies.name: Circuit Courts of Appeal
agencies.description: The U.S. Courts of Appeal hear appeals from lower courts of both civil and criminal trials, but do not investigate the facts of a case. Rather, the Appeals Courts investigate whether or not the law has been fairly and correctly applied by the lower courts.

agencies.name: Citizenship and Immigration Services        (USCIS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is responsible for processing immigration and naturalization applications and establishing policies regarding immigration services.

agencies.name: Civil Rights Division, Department of Justice
agencies.description: The Civil Rights Division is responsible for enforcing federal statutes that prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, disability or national origin.

agencies.name: Civil Rights, Department of Education Office of        (OCR)
agencies.description: The Office for Civil Rights (OCR) works to ensure equal access to education and resolve complaints of discrimination.

agencies.name: Commerce Department        (DOC)
agencies.description: The Department of Commerce (DOC) works with businesses, universities, communities, and the Nation’s workers to promote job creation, economic growth, sustainable development, and improved standards of living for Americans.

agencies.name: Commission of Fine Arts
agencies.description: The U. S. Commission of Fine Arts advises the government on matters pertaining to the arts, and to guide the architectural development of Washington.

agencies.name: Commission on Civil Rights        (USCCR)
agencies.description: The U.S. Commission on Civil Rights (USCCR) is an independent, bipartisan agency charged with monitoring federal civil rights enforcement.

agencies.name: Commission on International Religious Freedom        (USCIRF)
agencies.description: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) reviews the facts and circumstances of violations of religious freedom internationally and to make policy recommendations to the President, the Secretary of State and Congress.

agencies.name: Commission on Presidential Scholars
agencies.description: The Commission on Presidential Scholars selects and honors the Presidential Scholars, a group of graduating high school seniors of exceptional talent and commitment to public service.

agencies.name: Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe (Helsinki Commission)
agencies.description: The Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe monitors and encourages compliance with the Helsinki Final Act and other Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe commitments.

agencies.name: Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States        (CFIUS)
agencies.description: The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) reviews transactions that could result in control of a U.S. business by a foreign person.

agencies.name: Commodity Futures Trading Commission        (CFTC)
agencies.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) protects the public from fraud, manipulation, and abusive practices related to the sale of commodity and financial futures and options, and to fosters open, competitive, and financially sound futures and option markets. They investigate and prosecute commodities fraud, including foreign currency schemes, energy manipulation and hedge fund fraud, and works with other federal and state agencies to bring criminal and other actions.

agencies.name: Community Oriented Policing Services        (COPS)
agencies.description: The Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) advances the practice of community policing through sharing information and making grants to police departments in the United States.

agencies.name: Community Planning and Development        (CPD)
agencies.description: The Office of Community Planning and Development (CPD) develops communities by promoting decent housing, suitable living environments, and expanded economic opportunities for low and moderate income people.

agencies.name: Comptroller of the Currency, Office of        (OCC)
agencies.description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) charters, regulates, and supervises all national banks. It also supervises the federal branches and agencies of foreign banks.

agencies.name: Congressional Budget Office        (CBO)
agencies.description: The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) produces independent, nonpartisan, analysis of economic and budgetary issues to support the Congressional budget process.

agencies.name: Congressional Research Service        (CRS)
agencies.description: The Congressional Research Service (CRS) serves the Congress throughout the legislative process by providing comprehensive and reliable legislative research and analysis that are timely, objective, authoritative, and confidential, thereby contributing to an informed national legislature.

agencies.name: Congressional Workplace Rights, Office of        (OCWR)
agencies.description: The Office of Congressional Workplace Rights (OCWR) advances workplace rights, safety, health, and accessibility in the Legislative Branch.

agencies.name: Congress—U.S. House of Representatives
agencies.description: The U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate make up the two chambers of Congress. The House has 435 members, the number representing each state is determined by population.

agencies.name: Congress—U.S. Senate
agencies.description: The U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives make up the two chambers of Congress.  The Senate has 100 members, two from each state, who are elected to serve for a term of six years.

agencies.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau        (CFPB)
agencies.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) helps consumers by providing educational materials and accepting complaints. It supervises banks, lenders, and large non-bank entities, such as credit reporting agencies and debt collection companies. The Bureau also works to make credit card, mortgage, and other loan disclosures clearer, so consumers can understand their rights and responsibilities.

agencies.name: Coordinating Council on Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention
agencies.description: The Coordinating Council on Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention coordinates, studies the effectiveness of, and makes recommendations on juvenile crime prevention activities.

agencies.name: Copyright Office
agencies.description: The Copyright Office administers the national copyright system and provides advice on copyright law to congress, federal agencies, the courts and the public.

agencies.name: Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency        (CIGIE)
agencies.description: The Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) address integrity, economy, and effectiveness issues in the federal government.

agencies.name: Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency for the District of Columbia        (CSOSA)
agencies.description: The Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency (CSOSA) provides supervision of adults on parole, probation, and supervised release in the District of Columbia.

agencies.name: Customs and Border Protection        (CBP)
agencies.description: Customs and Border Protection (CBP) prevents people from entering the country illegally or bringing anything harmful or illegal into the United States.

agencies.name: Cyber Command
agencies.description: The U.S. Cyber Command coordinates cyberspace operations to defend U.S. interests.

agencies.name: Debt and Claims Management Center
agencies.description: The Debt and Claims Management Center collects or settles delinquent debts for the Department of Defense by former military members and civilian employees.

agencies.name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency        (DARPA)
agencies.description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) serves as the central research and development organization of the Department of Defense.

agencies.name: Defense Contract Audit Agency        (DCAA)
agencies.description: The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) audits U.S. Department of Defense contracts.

agencies.name: Defense Contract Management Agency        (DCMA)
agencies.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCAMA) is responsible for contract management for the Department of Defense, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, and several other federal, state, foreign and international governments and agencies. Its goal is to ensure contracts are fulfilled on time and at the correct cost.

agencies.name: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency        (DCSA)
agencies.description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) provides industrial security engagement and counterintelligence support to secure the trustworthiness of the U.S. government's workforce, contract support, technologies, services, and supply chains.

agencies.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service        (DFAS)
agencies.description: The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) oversees payments to Department of Defense servicemembers, employees, vendors and contractors. The Defense Finance and Accounting Services also provides Department of Defense decision makers with business intelligence, finance and accounting information.

agencies.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service Debt and Claims Management Center
agencies.description: The Debt and Claims Management Center collects or settles delinquent debts for the Department of Defense by former military members and civilian employees.

agencies.name: Defense Intelligence Agency        (DIA)
agencies.description: The Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) provides defense intelligence to war fighters, planners, and policy makers.

agencies.name: Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board        (DNFSB)
agencies.description: The Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board (DNFSB) reviews the content and implementation of health and safety standards at Department of Energy Defense Nuclear Facilities. The board also makes recommendations to the President and Secretary of Energy regarding health and safety issues at Defense Nuclear Facilities.

agencies.name: Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency        (DPAA)
agencies.description: The Department of Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) works to recover service members who became missing during their service.

agencies.name: Defense Security Cooperation Agency        (DSCA)
agencies.description: The Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) supports U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. They train, educate, advise, and equip foreign security forces to respond to shared challenges.

agencies.name: Defense Technical Information Center        (DTIC)
agencies.description: The Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC) serves the Department of Defense as a repository of government funded scientific, technical, engineering and business related information.

agencies.name: Defense Threat Reduction Agency        (DTRA)
agencies.description: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) is a combat support agency whose goal is to reduce the threat posed by weapons of mass destruction.

agencies.name: Denali Commission
agencies.description: The Denali Commission provides critical utilities, infrastructure, and economic support throughout Alaska.

agencies.name: Department of Agriculture        (USDA)
agencies.description: The Department of Agriculture (USDA) provides leadership on food, agriculture, natural resources, and related issues.

agencies.name: Department of Commerce        (DOC)
agencies.description: The Department of Commerce (DOC) works with businesses, universities, communities, and the Nation’s workers to promote job creation, economic growth, sustainable development, and improved standards of living for Americans.

agencies.name: Department of Education        (ED)
agencies.description: The Department of Education (ED) fosters educational excellence, and to ensures equal access to educational opportunity for all.

agencies.name: Department of Energy        (DOE)
agencies.description: The Department of Energy (DOE) manages the United States' nuclear infrastructure and administers the country's energy policy. The Department of Energy also funds scientific research in the field.

agencies.name: Department of Energy’s Office of Science
agencies.description: The Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Office of Science supports scientific research in 10 of the Department of Energy's National Laboratories. The Science Office also operates several open-access scientific facilities that are available for projects of sufficient scientific merit.

agencies.name: Department of Homeland Security        (DHS)
agencies.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) works to improve the security of the United States. The Department's work includes customs, border, and immigration enforcement, emergency response to natural and manmade disasters, antiterrorism work, and cybersecurity.

agencies.name: Department of Housing and Urban Development        (HUD)
agencies.description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) administers programs that provide housing and community development assistance. The Department also works to ensure fair and equal housing opportunity for all.

agencies.name: Department of Justice        (DOJ)
agencies.description: The Department of Justice (DOJ) enforces federal laws, seeks just punishment for the guilty, and ensures the fair and impartial administration of justice.

agencies.name: Department of Labor        (DOL)
agencies.description: The Department of Labor (DOL) administers federal labor laws to guarantee workers' rights to fair, safe, and healthy working conditions, including minimum hourly wage and overtime pay, protection against employment discrimination, and unemployment insurance.

agencies.name: Department of Veterans Affairs        (VA)
agencies.description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) runs programs benefiting veterans and members of their families. It offers education opportunities and rehabilitation services and provides compensation payments for disabilities or death related to military service, home loan guaranties, pensions, burials, and health care that includes the services of nursing homes, clinics, and medical centers.

agencies.name: Department of the Interior        (DOI)
agencies.description: The Department of the Interior (DOI) manages public lands and minerals, national parks, and wildlife refuges and upholds Federal trust responsibilities to Indian tribes and Native Alaskans. Additionally, Interior is responsible for endangered species conservation and other environmental conservation efforts.

agencies.name: Department of the Treasury
agencies.description: The Department of the Treasury manages federal finances by collecting taxes and paying bills and by managing currency, government accounts and public debt. The Department of the Treasury also enforces finance and tax laws.

agencies.name: Disability Employment Policy, Office of        (ODEP)
agencies.description: The Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP) creates policies to ensure that people with disabilities are fully integrated in the workforce.

agencies.name: Economic Research Service        (ERS)
agencies.description: The Economic Research Service (ERS) provides the Department of Agriculture and the public economic information and research on food, agriculture, the environment and rural development.

agencies.name: Education Department        (ED)
agencies.description: The Department of Education (ED) fosters educational excellence, and to ensures equal access to educational opportunity for all.

agencies.name: Elder Justice Initiative        (EJI)
agencies.description: The Elder Justice Initiative (EJI) supports and coordinates the Department of Justice's efforts to combat elder abuse, neglect, and financial fraud and scams that target our nation’s seniors.

agencies.name: Election Assistance Commission        (EAC)
agencies.description: The Election Assistance Commission (EAC) supports state and local election officials in their efforts to ensure accessible, accurate. and secure elections. EAC develops guidance to meet the Help America Vote Act requirements, adopts voluntary voting system guidelines, and serves as a national clearinghouse of information on election administration. EAC also accredits testing laboratories and certifies voting systems, as well as audits the use of Help America Vote Act funds.

agencies.name: Elementary and Secondary Education, Office of        (OESE)
agencies.description: The Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE) works to improve the achievement of students in preschool through secondary school. The office also works to ensure equal education opportunities for all, and to provide assistance to state and local schools.

agencies.name: Employee Benefits Security Administration        (EBSA)
agencies.description: The Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA) offers information and assistance on employer-sponsored retirement benefit and health benefit plans.

agencies.name: Employment and Training Administration        (ETA)
agencies.description: The Employment and Training Administration (ETA) provides job training and help with finding jobs and careers.

agencies.name: Energy Department        (DOE)
agencies.description: The Department of Energy (DOE) manages the United States' nuclear infrastructure and administers the country's energy policy. The Department of Energy also funds scientific research in the field.

agencies.name: Engraving and Printing, Bureau of        (BEP)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) produces United States currency notes, operates as the nation's central bank, and serves to ensure that adequate amounts of currency and coin are in circulation.

agencies.name: Environmental Management, Office of
agencies.description: The Office of Environmental Management cleans up nuclear weapons test sites and government sponsored nuclear energy research sites.

agencies.name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission        (EEOC)
agencies.description: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) enforces laws that make discrimination illegal in the workplace. The commission oversees all types of work situations including hiring, firing, promotions, harassment, training, wages, and benefits.

agencies.name: Executive Office for Immigration Review        (EOIR)
agencies.description: The Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) administers the immigration court system, which decides whether an individual charged with violating immigration law should be allowed to stay in the country or not.

agencies.name: Export-Import Bank of the United States        (EXIM)
agencies.description: The Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) assists American businesses export their goods by providing financial assistance in the form of loans, loan guarantees and insurance. The focus of the Export-Import Bank is on assisting small businesses.

agencies.name: Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity        (FHEO)
agencies.description: The Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO) enforces federal laws and establishes policies to ensure that all Americans have equal access to the housing of their choice.

agencies.name: Fannie Mae
agencies.description: Fannie Mae purchases mortgages from lending institutions in an effort to increase affordable lending activity at those institutions. Fannie Mae is not a federal agency. It is a government-sponsored enterprise under the conservatorship of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA).

agencies.name: Farm Credit Administration        (FCA)
agencies.description: The Farm Credit Administration (FCA) is an independent financial regulatory agency that oversees the Farm Credit System, a nationwide network of lending institutions that serve farmers, ranchers, agricultural cooperatives, and other eligible borrowers. It also oversees the Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corporation or Farmer Mac, which provides a secondary market for agricultural real estate mortgage loans, rural housing loans, and rural cooperative loans.

agencies.name: Farm Credit System Insurance Corporation        (FCSIC)
agencies.description: The Farm Credit System Insurance Corporation (FCSIC) ensures the payment of principal and interest on insured notes, bonds, and other obligations issued on behalf of Farm Credit System.

agencies.name: FedStats        (FCSM)
agencies.description: The Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) was founded in 1975 by the Statistical and Science Policy Branch (formerly, the Office of Statistical Policy) in the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to assist in carrying out SSP/OMB's role in setting and coordinating statistical policy.

agencies.name: Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board        (FASAB)
agencies.description: The Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board (FASAB) serves the public interest by improving federal financial reporting through issuing federal financial accounting standards and providing guidance after considering the needs of external and internal users of federal financial information.

agencies.name: Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology        (FCSM)
agencies.description: The Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) was founded in 1975 by the Statistical and Science Policy Branch (formerly, the Office of Statistical Policy) in the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to assist in carrying out SSP/OMB's role in setting and coordinating statistical policy.

agencies.name: Federal Consulting Group        (FCG)
agencies.description: The Federal Consulting Group (FCG) offers consulting, executive coaching, and performance and customer satisfaction measuring services to federal agencies.

agencies.name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation        (FDIC)
agencies.description: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) answers questions about federal deposit insurance coverage, and handles complaints and inquiries about FDIC-insured state banks which are not members of the Federal Reserve System.

agencies.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission        (FERC)
agencies.description: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) regulates interstate transmission of electricity, natural gas, and oil, and also regulates hydropower projects and natural gas terminals.

agencies.name: Federal Executive Boards        (FEBs)
agencies.description: Federal Executive Boards (FEBs) operate in 28 US cities and provide a forum for collaboration and information exchange between federal field agencies. In this way, field agencies may share best practices and lessons learned, or may coordinate efforts when different agencies adopt programs with similar goals.

agencies.name: Federal Financing Bank        (FFB)
agencies.description: The Federal Financing Bank (FFB) was created to centralize, reduce the cost of, and efficiently manage federal borrowing.

agencies.name: Federal Geographic Data Committee        (FGDC)
agencies.description: The Federal Geographic Data Committee (FGDC) is an interagency group that promotes and coordinates the production, use, and publication of geospatial data.

agencies.name: Federal Housing Administration        (FHA)
agencies.description: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) provides mortgage insurance on single-family, multifamily, manufactured home, and hospital loans made by FHA-approved lenders throughout the United States and its territories.

agencies.name: Federal Housing Finance Agency        (FHFA)
agencies.description: The Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) provides supervision, regulation, and housing mission oversight of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and the Federal Home Loan Banks.

agencies.name: Federal Judicial Center
agencies.description: The Federal Judicial Center conducts policy research and provides continuing education resources for the judicial branch.

agencies.name: Federal Labor Relations Authority        (FLRA)
agencies.description: The Federal Labor Relations Authority (FLRA) is a quasi-judicial body that manages relations between federal agencies and employees.

agencies.name: Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers        (FLETC)
agencies.description: The Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC), through strategic partnerships, prepares the federal law enforcement community to safeguard America’s people, property, and institutions.

agencies.name: Federal Library and Information Network         (FEDLINK)
agencies.description: The Federal Library and Information Network (FEDLINK) coordinates and shares available resources to provide continuing education and training to federal library and information center employees.

agencies.name: Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission
agencies.description: The Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission is an independent agency that administers trials and hears appeals of disputes relating directly to the Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977.

agencies.name: Federal Protective Service        (FPS)
agencies.description: The Federal Protective Service (FPS) is a federal law enforcement agency that provides security and law enforcement services to federally owned and leased buildings.

agencies.name: Federal Register        (OFR)
agencies.description: The Office of the Federal Register (OFR) oversees the Federal Register publication system, making available the full text of federal laws and regulations, presidential documents, and other federal program information.

agencies.name: Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board        (FRTIB)
agencies.description: The Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board (FRTIB) administers the Thrift Savings Plan, a tax-deferred retirement account similar to a 401(k).

agencies.name: Fiscal Service, Bureau of the
agencies.description: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service manages all federal payments and collections, and provides government-wide accounting and reporting services. You can contact them to buy bonds or to check on the maturity of bonds you own.

agencies.name: Fish and Wildlife Service        (FWS)
agencies.description: The Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) works to conserve, protect and enhance fish, wildlife and plants and their habitats.

agencies.name: Fleet Forces Command        (USFFC)
agencies.description: U.S. Fleet Forces Command (USFFC) organizes, staffs, trains, maintains, and equips Navy forces, and develops fleet readiness.

agencies.name: Food and Nutrition Service        (FNS)
agencies.description: The Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) provides children and low-income people access to food, a healthful diet, and nutrition education.

agencies.name: Foreign Claims Settlement Commission        (FCSC)
agencies.description: The Foreign Claims Settlement Commission (FCSC) is a quasi-judicial body that hears claims cases brought by U.S. nationals against foreign governments. The jurisdiction of the body is specific, and its decisions are final.

agencies.name: Fossil Energy        (FECM)
agencies.description: The Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management (FECM) is responsible for research and development of programs involving coal, petroleum, and natural gas.

agencies.name: Fulbright Program
agencies.description: The Fulbright Program offers grants to study, teach and conduct research for U.S. citizens to go abroad, and non-U.S. citizens to come to the United States.

agencies.name: General Services Administration        (GSA)
agencies.description: The General Services Administration (GSA) manages federal property and provides contracting options for government agencies.

agencies.name: Geological Survey        (USGS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Geological Survey  (USGS) is the nation's largest water, earth, and biological science and civilian mapping agency. It collects, monitors, analyzes, and provides scientific understanding of natural resource conditions, issues, and problems.

agencies.name: Ginnie Mae
agencies.description: Ginnie Mae is a self-financing, wholly owned U.S. Government corporation within the Department of Housing and Urban Development. It is the primary financing mechanism for all government-insured or government-guaranteed mortgage loans.

agencies.name: Global Media, Agency for
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media, formerly known as the Broadcasting Board of Governors, broadcasts news and information about the United States and the world to audiences abroad.

agencies.name: Government Accountability Office        (GAO)
agencies.description: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) gathers information to help Congress determine how effectively executive branch agencies are doing their jobs.

agencies.name: Government Ethics, Office of        (OGE)
agencies.description: The Office of Government Ethics (OGE) provides oversight, policy, and guidance to the Executive Branch regarding ethics laws and policies.

agencies.name: Government Publishing Office        (GPO)
agencies.description: The Government Publishing Office (GPO) publishes and distributes official government publications to Congress, federal agencies, federal depository libraries, and the public. Anyone may use the services of a federal depository library to access government publications.

agencies.name: Helsinki Commission
agencies.description: The Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe monitors and encourages compliance with the Helsinki Final Act and other Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe commitments.

agencies.name: Homeland Security Department        (DHS)
agencies.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) works to improve the security of the United States. The Department's work includes customs, border, and immigration enforcement, emergency response to natural and manmade disasters, antiterrorism work, and cybersecurity.

agencies.name: Hour and Wage Division        (WHD)
agencies.description: The Division of Hours and Wages (WHD) is responsible for enforcing the country's labor laws, including those related to the minimum wage and employment of minors.

agencies.name: House Office of Inspector General        (OIG)
agencies.description: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) conducts audits of the financial and administrative operations of the House of Representatives.

agencies.name: House Office of the Clerk
agencies.description: The Office of the Clerk performs administrative functions for the U.S. House of Representatives, including creating and retaining the House Journal, calling new members to order, tracking questions of order, and managing the offices and staff of deceased or retired representatives.

agencies.name: House of Representatives
agencies.description: The U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate make up the two chambers of Congress. The House has 435 members, the number representing each state is determined by population.

agencies.name: Housing Office
agencies.description: The Office of Housing regulates the housing industry and administers the Federal Housing Administration. The regulatory programs administered by the Office of Housing include single family housing and multifamily housing programs.

agencies.name: Housing and Urban Development, Department of        (HUD)
agencies.description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) administers programs that provide housing and community development assistance. The Department also works to ensure fair and equal housing opportunity for all.

agencies.name: Immigrant and Employee Rights Section        (IER)
agencies.description: The Immigrant and Employee Rights Section (IER) is responsible for protecting immigrants authorized to work in the U.S. against employment discrimination.

agencies.name: Immigration and Citizenship Services        (USCIS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is responsible for processing immigration and naturalization applications and establishing policies regarding immigration services.

agencies.name: Immigration and Customs Enforcement        (ICE)
agencies.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforces federal laws governing border control, customs, trade, and immigration.

agencies.name: Indian Affairs        (BIA)
agencies.description: The mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) is to enhance the quality of life, to promote economic opportunity, and to carry out the responsibility to protect and improve the trust assets of American Indians, Indian tribes, and Alaska Natives.

agencies.name: Indian Arts and Crafts Board        (IACB)
agencies.description: The Indian Arts and Crafts Board (IACB) enforces the Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990 that prohibits false advertising in the marketing of Indian arts or crafts. The Board also provides certified Indian-owned business listings, provides federally recognized tribes with business assistance, and operates several Indian Arts and Crafts museums.

agencies.name: Indian Health Service        (IHS)
agencies.description: The Indian Health Service (IHS) provides federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives.

agencies.name: Indo-Pacific Command        (USINDOPACOM)
agencies.description: The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM) is responsible for defending and promoting U.S. interests in the Pacific and Asia.

agencies.name: Inspectors General        (CIGIE)
agencies.description: The Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) address integrity, economy, and effectiveness issues in the federal government.

agencies.name: Institute of Education Sciences        (IES)
agencies.description: The Institute of Education Sciences (IES) provides rigorous evidence on which to base educational policy and practices.

agencies.name: Institute of Museum and Library Services        (IMLS)
agencies.description: The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) is a grant making organization that also conducts research and develops policy. The Institute helps libraries and museums innovate, fosters lifelong learning and cultural and civic engagement.

agencies.name: Inter-American Foundation        (IAF)
agencies.description: The Inter-American Foundation (IAF) provides grant support to Latin American and Caribbean grass-roots groups and non-governmental organizations with creative self-help ideas.

agencies.name: Interior Department        (DOI)
agencies.description: The Department of the Interior (DOI) manages public lands and minerals, national parks, and wildlife refuges and upholds Federal trust responsibilities to Indian tribes and Native Alaskans. Additionally, Interior is responsible for endangered species conservation and other environmental conservation efforts.

agencies.name: Internal Revenue Service        (IRS)
agencies.description: The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) administers and enforces U.S. federal tax laws.

agencies.name: International Development Finance Corporation        (DFC)
agencies.description: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is America’s development bank. DFC partners with the private sector to finance solutions to the most critical challenges facing the developing world.

agencies.name: International Labor Affairs, Bureau of        (ILAB)
agencies.description: The Bureau of International Labor Affairs (ILAB) works to improve working conditions, raise living standards, protect workers’ ability to exercise their rights, and address the workplace exploitation of children and other vulnerable populations.

agencies.name: International Trade Administration        (ITA)
agencies.description: The International Trade Administration (ITA) promotes U.S. exports by providing diplomatic support, helping to shape trade policy, removing trade barriers, and enforcing U.S. trade laws and agreements.

agencies.name: Interpol
agencies.description: Interpol Washington, the U.S. National Central Bureau, coordinates law enforcement activities between U.S. agencies and their international counterparts.

agencies.name: James Madison Memorial Fellowship Foundation
agencies.description: The James Madison Memorial Fellowship Foundation offers fellowship opportunities to individuals who are seeking a Master's degree in order to teach secondary students about the U.S. Constitution.

agencies.name: Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries
agencies.description: The Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries specifies the standards and qualifications an individual must meet in order to perform actuarial services.

agencies.name: Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies        (JCCIC)
agencies.description: Made up of members of the House and Senate, the Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies (JCCIC) is responsible for planning and carrying out the President's swearing-in ceremony at the U.S. Capitol.

agencies.name: Joint Forces Staff College        (JFSC)
agencies.description: The Joint Forces Staff College (JFSC) trains military and civilian decision makers in joint operations planning, strategy, and management.

agencies.name: Joint Program Executive Office for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense        (JPEO-CBRND)
agencies.description: The Joint Program Executive Office for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (JPEO-CBRND) works to deter, detect, and if necessary, deal with the consequences of a weapon of mass destruction attack.

agencies.name: Judicial Circuit Courts of Appeal
agencies.description: The U.S. Courts of Appeal hear appeals from lower courts of both civil and criminal trials, but do not investigate the facts of a case. Rather, the Appeals Courts investigate whether or not the law has been fairly and correctly applied by the lower courts.

agencies.name: Justice Department        (DOJ)
agencies.description: The Department of Justice (DOJ) enforces federal laws, seeks just punishment for the guilty, and ensures the fair and impartial administration of justice.

agencies.name: Justice Programs, Office of        (OJP)
agencies.description: The Office of Justice Programs (OJP) is a research and grant-making organization that works to provide local and state law enforcement agencies with information, training, coordination, and innovative strategies for dealing with the most pressing law enforcement issues.

agencies.name: Labor Department        (DOL)
agencies.description: The Department of Labor (DOL) administers federal labor laws to guarantee workers' rights to fair, safe, and healthy working conditions, including minimum hourly wage and overtime pay, protection against employment discrimination, and unemployment insurance.

agencies.name: Land Management, Bureau of        (BLM)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) manages outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production on public lands.

agencies.name: Legal Services Corporation
agencies.description: The Legal Services Corporation is an independent corporation founded by Congress that provides grant funds, training, and technical assistance to civil legal aid programs. The Corporation ensures low income individuals and families have access to quality legal aid.

agencies.name: Library of Congress
agencies.description: The Library of Congress provides Congress with objective research to inform the legislative process, administers the national copyright system, and manages the largest collection of books, recordings, photographs, maps and manuscripts in the world.

agencies.name: Manufactured Housing Programs, Office of        (OMHP)
agencies.description: The Manufactured Housing Program (OMHP) is a consumer protection program that regulates the construction of certain factory-built housing units called "manufactured homes".

agencies.name: Marine Corps
agencies.description: The Marine Corps is a branch of the United States Armed Forces responsible for delivering task forces on land, at sea, and in the air.

agencies.name: Medicaid        (CMS)
agencies.description: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) provides health coverage to more than 100 million people through Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, and the Health Insurance Marketplace. The CMS seeks to strengthen and modernize the Nation’s health care system, to provide access to high quality care and improved health at lower costs.

agencies.name: Medicaid and CHIP Payment and Access Commission        (MACPAC)
agencies.description: The Medicaid and CHIP Payment and Access Commission (MACPAC) reviews federal and state medicaid and CHIP policies and makes recommendations to Congress, the department of health and human services, and the states.

agencies.name: Medicare        (CMS)
agencies.description: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) provides health coverage to more than 100 million people through Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, and the Health Insurance Marketplace. The CMS seeks to strengthen and modernize the Nation’s health care system, to provide access to high quality care and improved health at lower costs.

agencies.name: Medicare Payment Advisory Commission        (MedPAC)
agencies.description: The Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) advises Congress on a range of issues affecting Medicare, including payments, services, access, and regulations.

agencies.name: Merit Systems Protection Board        (MSPB)
agencies.description: The Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) hears appeals from federal employees, and studies federal merit systems in an effort to protect the rights of federal employees.

agencies.name: Migratory Bird Conservation Commission
agencies.description: The Migratory Bird Conservation Commission considers and approves areas of land or water recommended by the Secretary of the Interior for purchase or rental by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

agencies.name: Mine Safety and Health Administration        (MSHA)
agencies.description: The Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) works to prevent mining related deaths, injuries, and illnesses through mine regulations, inspections, and training programs.

agencies.name: Minority Health, Office of        (OMH)
agencies.description: The Office of Minority Health (OMH) improves the health of racial and ethnic minority populations through the development of health policies and programs.

agencies.name: Mississippi River Commission        (MRC)
agencies.description: The Mississippi River Commission (MRC) researches and provides policy and work recommendations in the areas of flood control, navigation, and environmental projects.

agencies.name: NOAA Fisheries
agencies.description: NOAA Fisheries, also known as the National Marine Fisheries Service, is responsible for the management, conservation, and protection of living marine resources within about 200 miles of the U.S. coast.

agencies.name: National Aeronautics and Space Administration        (NASA)
agencies.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) explores space, and researches Earth systems, the solar system, and the universe.

agencies.name: National Archives and Records Administration        (NARA)
agencies.description: The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) preserves U.S. government records, manages the Presidential Libraries system, and publishes laws, regulations, Presidential, and other public documents.

agencies.name: National Cancer Institute        (NCI)
agencies.description: The National Cancer Institute (NCI) conducts and supports research, training, health information distribution, and other programs related to the cause, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cancer, rehabilitation from cancer, and the continuing care of cancer patients and the families of cancer patients.

agencies.name: National Cemetery Administration        (NCA)
agencies.description: The National Cemetery Administration (NCA) provides burial space for Veterans and their eligible family members, and maintains national cemeteries as national shrines, sacred to the honor and memory of those interred or memorialized there.

agencies.name: National Council on Disability        (NCD)
agencies.description: The National Council on Disability (NCD) makes recommendations to the President and Congress on policies affecting Americans with disabilities. They empower individuals with disabilities and promote equal opportunity.

agencies.name: National Credit Union Administration        (NCUA)
agencies.description: The National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) charters and supervises federal credit unions and insures savings in federal and most state-chartered credit unions.

agencies.name: National Defense University        (NDU)
agencies.description: The National Defense University (NDU) provides educational opportunities for military personnel and civilians.

agencies.name: National Endowment for the Arts        (NEA)
agencies.description: The National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) funds, promotes, and strengthens the creative capacity of our communities by providing all Americans with opportunities for arts participation.

agencies.name: National Endowment for the Humanities        (NEH)
agencies.description: The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) funds humanities programs in the United States such as museums, archives, libraries, colleges, universities, public television, radio stations, and individual scholars.

agencies.name: National Flood Insurance Program        (NFIP)
agencies.description: National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) provides affordable insurance to property owners and encourages communities to adopt and enforce floodplain management regulations.

agencies.name: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency        (NGA)
agencies.description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) provides location-based intelligence in support of national security.

agencies.name: National Guard
agencies.description: The National Guard provides trained units to the states, territories and the District of Columbia to protect life and property. The Guard also provides trained units to defend the United States and its interests all over the globe.

agencies.name: National Health Information Center        (NHIC)
agencies.description: The National Health Information Center (NHIC) helps connect health professionals and consumers to the organizations that can best answer their questions by providing up-to-date contact information for the most reliable resources.

agencies.name: National Indian Gaming Commission
agencies.description: The National Indian Gaming Commission is a regulatory body that oversees some aspects of gaming on Indian lands, often complementing the work of Indian regulators.

agencies.name: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health        (NIOSH)
agencies.description: The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) conducts research and makes recommendations for the prevention of work-related injury and illness.

agencies.name: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases        (NIAID)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) provides health information on allergic, infectious, and immunologic diseases. Diseases include food allergy, sinusitis, and genital herpes. Consumers can call or write to the institute with questions and can order publications over the phone or on the Web site.

agencies.name: National Institute of Corrections        (NIC)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Corrections (NIC) gives training, technical assistance, and information services to federal, state, and local corrections facilities.

agencies.name: National Institute of Deafness and Other Communication Disorders        (NIDCD)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) supports biomedical and behavioral research on hearing, balance, smell, taste, voice, speech and language.

agencies.name: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases        (NIDDK)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) supports the research of diabetes, digestive diseases, kidney diseases, and more.

agencies.name: National Institute of Mental Health        (NIMH)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) conducts and supports research that seeks to understand, treat, and prevent mental illness.

agencies.name: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke        (NINDS)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) investigates the causes, prevention, diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases such as cerebral palsy, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, autism, and stroke.

agencies.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology        (NIST)
agencies.description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes U.S. innovation and industrial competitiveness by advancing measurement science, standards, and technology in ways that enhance economic security and improve our quality of life.

agencies.name: National Institutes of Health        (NIH)
agencies.description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is the primary Federal agency for conducting and supporting medical research.

agencies.name: National Interagency Fire Center        (NIFC)
agencies.description: The National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) coordinates the national mobilization of resources for wildland fire and other incidents throughout the United States.

agencies.name: National Laboratories
agencies.description: The National Laboratories conduct scientific research and development in areas related to energy and technology.

agencies.name: National Marine Fisheries Service
agencies.description: NOAA Fisheries, also known as the National Marine Fisheries Service, is responsible for the management, conservation, and protection of living marine resources within about 200 miles of the U.S. coast.

agencies.name: National Nuclear Security Administration        (NNSA)
agencies.description: The National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) works to ensure that the nation's stockpile of nuclear weapons is safe and secure. It also works to ensure the safety of naval nuclear reactors, is the first responder in case of nuclear emergency, and works on worldwide nuclear nonproliferation issues.

agencies.name: National Ocean Service
agencies.description: The National Ocean Service (NOS) provides data, tools, and services that support coastal economies and their contribution to the national economy.

agencies.name: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration        (NOAA)
agencies.description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) works to understand and predict changes in climate, weather, oceans, and coasts. Their work supports severe weather preparedness, and international shipping.

agencies.name: National Park Foundation        (NPF)
agencies.description: The National Park Foundation (NPF) supports America’s national parks through conservation, preservation, education, and community engagement.

agencies.name: National Park Service        (NPS)
agencies.description: The National Park Service (NPS) cares for the more than 400 national parks in the United States. The National Park Service partners with local communities to assist in historic preservation and the creation and maintenance of recreational spaces.

agencies.name: National Pesticide Information Center        (NPIC)
agencies.description: The National Pesticide Information Center (NPIC) provides objective, science-based information about a wide variety of pesticide-related subjects, including pesticide products, pesticide poisonings, toxicology, and environmental chemistry.

agencies.name: National Prevention Information Network        (NPIN)
agencies.description: The CDC National Prevention Information Network (NPIN) is the reference and referral service for information on HIV/AIDS, viral hepatitis, sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), and tuberculosis (TB).

agencies.name: National Science Foundation        (NSF)
agencies.description: The National Science Foundation (NSF) supports research and education across all fields of science and technology, primarily through grants.

agencies.name: National Technical Information Service        (NTIS)
agencies.description: The National Technical Information Service (NTIS) provides businesses, universities, and the public access to government-funded scientific, engineering, technical, and business related information.

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board        (NTSB)
agencies.description: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigates every civil aviation accident in the U.S. and significant accidents in other modes of transportation. Based on their investigative findings and special studies, the board makes recommendations aimed at preventing future accidents.

agencies.name: Navy
agencies.description: The Navy's primary mission is to defend the United States.

agencies.name: Northern Border Regional Commission
agencies.description: The Northern Border Regional Commission is a federal-state partnership for economic, and community development in northern Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, and New York.

agencies.name: Northern Command        (USNORTHCOM)
agencies.description: The U.S Northern Command (USNORTHCOM) is responsible for defending the continental United States and Alaska, and for coordinating with the defenses of Canada, Mexico, and the Bahamas.

agencies.name: Nuclear Energy, Office of
agencies.description: The Office of Nuclear Energy works to improve the safety, cost, security, and efficiency of nuclear energy generation.

agencies.name: Nuclear Waste Technical Review Board        (NWTRB)
agencies.description: The Nuclear Waste Technical Review Board (NWTRB) provides scientific and technical oversight of the Department of Energy's program for managing and disposing of high-level nuclear waste and spent nuclear fuel.

agencies.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory        (ORNL)
agencies.description: The Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) conducts world-leading research in advanced materials exploration, alternative fuels, clean energy, and supercomputing.

agencies.name: Ocean Energy Management, Bureau of        (BOEM)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) promotes energy independence, environmental protection, and economic development by managing offshore energy resources.

agencies.name: Office for Civil Rights, Department of Education        (OCR)
agencies.description: The Office for Civil Rights (OCR) works to ensure equal access to education and resolve complaints of discrimination.

agencies.name: Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education        (OCTAE)
agencies.description: The Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education (OCTAE) administers and coordinates programs that are related to adult education and literacy, career and technical education, and community colleges.

agencies.name: Office of Child Support Services         (OCSS)
agencies.description: The Office of Child Support Services (OCSS) assures that support (both financial and medical) is available to children through locating parents, establishing paternity, identifying support obligations, and enforcing those obligations.

agencies.name: Office of Community Planning and Development        (CPD)
agencies.description: The Office of Community Planning and Development (CPD) develops communities by promoting decent housing, suitable living environments, and expanded economic opportunities for low and moderate income people.

agencies.name: Office of Congressional Workplace Rights        (OCWR)
agencies.description: The Office of Congressional Workplace Rights (OCWR) advances workplace rights, safety, health, and accessibility in the Legislative Branch.

agencies.name: Office of Cuba Broadcasting        (Radio y TV Martí)
agencies.description: The Office of Cuba Broadcasting provides the Cuban people with news and information.

agencies.name: Office of Disability Employment Policy        (ODEP)
agencies.description: The Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP) creates policies to ensure that people with disabilities are fully integrated in the workforce.

agencies.name: Office of Elementary and Secondary Education        (OESE)
agencies.description: The Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE) works to improve the achievement of students in preschool through secondary school. The office also works to ensure equal education opportunities for all, and to provide assistance to state and local schools.

agencies.name: Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy        (EERE)
agencies.description: The Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE) answers questions about EEREs products, services, and technology programs, and refers callers to the most appropriate EERE resources.

agencies.name: Office of English Language Acquisition
agencies.description: Part of the Department of Education, the Office of English Language Acquisition (OELA) supports programs for students learning English.

agencies.name: Office of Environmental Management
agencies.description: The Office of Environmental Management cleans up nuclear weapons test sites and government sponsored nuclear energy research sites.

agencies.name: Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity        (FHEO)
agencies.description: The Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO) enforces federal laws and establishes policies to ensure that all Americans have equal access to the housing of their choice.

agencies.name: Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management         (FECM)
agencies.description: The Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management (FECM) is responsible for research and development of programs involving coal, petroleum, and natural gas.

agencies.name: Office of Government Ethics        (OGE)
agencies.description: The Office of Government Ethics (OGE) provides oversight, policy, and guidance to the Executive Branch regarding ethics laws and policies.

agencies.name: Office of Housing
agencies.description: The Office of Housing regulates the housing industry and administers the Federal Housing Administration. The regulatory programs administered by the Office of Housing include single family housing and multifamily housing programs.

agencies.name: Office of Immigrant and Employee Rights        (IER)
agencies.description: The Immigrant and Employee Rights Section (IER) is responsible for protecting immigrants authorized to work in the U.S. against employment discrimination.

agencies.name: Office of Justice Programs        (OJP)
agencies.description: The Office of Justice Programs (OJP) is a research and grant-making organization that works to provide local and state law enforcement agencies with information, training, coordination, and innovative strategies for dealing with the most pressing law enforcement issues.

agencies.name: Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes        (OLHCHH)
agencies.description: The Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes (OLHCHH) works to make private homes safe from lead and other harmful materials.

agencies.name: Office of Manufactured Housing Programs        (OMHP)
agencies.description: The Manufactured Housing Program (OMHP) is a consumer protection program that regulates the construction of certain factory-built housing units called "manufactured homes".

agencies.name: Office of Minority Health        (OMH)
agencies.description: The Office of Minority Health (OMH) improves the health of racial and ethnic minority populations through the development of health policies and programs.

agencies.name: Office of Multifamily Housing Programs        (MFH)
agencies.description: The Office of Multifamily Housing (MFH) Programs administers the Department of Housing and Urban Development's multifamily housing programs through a network of local offices across the country.

agencies.name: Office of Nuclear Energy
agencies.description: The Office of Nuclear Energy works to improve the safety, cost, security, and efficiency of nuclear energy generation.

agencies.name: Office of Personnel Management        (OPM)
agencies.description: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) manages the civil service of the federal government, coordinates recruiting of new government employees, and manages their health insurance and retirement benefits programs. They also provide resources for locating student jobs, summer jobs, scholarships, and internships.

agencies.name: Office of Policy Development and Research (PD&R)
agencies.description: The Office of Policy Development and Research (PD&R) provides the Department of Housing and Urban Development up-to-date information and analysis of housing and community development issues.

agencies.name: Office of Refugee Resettlement        (ORR)
agencies.description: The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) promotes the health, well-being, and stability of refugees, unaccompanied children, and other eligible individuals and families through culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based services.

agencies.name: Office of Servicemember Affairs
agencies.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Office of Servicemember Affairs (OSA) addresses consumer financial challenges affecting military members, veterans, and their families.

agencies.name: Office of Special Counsel        (OSC)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Counsel (OSC) is an investigative and prosecutorial office that works to end government and political corruption, and to protect government employees and whistleblowers.

agencies.name: Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services        (OSERS)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) provides a wide array of supports to parents, students, school districts, and states in three main areas: special education, vocational rehabilitation, and research.

agencies.name: Office of Surface Mining, Reclamation and Enforcement        (OSMRE)
agencies.description: The Office of Surface Mining, Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) protects populations and the environment during surface coal mining operations. The Office also works to clean and put to good use abandoned mine sites. These missions are accomplished primarily through regulation and oversight of state programs.

agencies.name: Office of Textiles and Apparel         (OTEXA)
agencies.description: The Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA) works on textile trade policy, and textile trade agreements.

agencies.name: Office of Weights and Measures         (OWM)
agencies.description: The Office of Weights and Measures (OWM) promotes uniformity in U.S. weights and measures laws, regulations, and standards to achieve equity between buyers and sellers in the marketplace.

agencies.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency        (OCC)
agencies.description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) charters, regulates, and supervises all national banks. It also supervises the federal branches and agencies of foreign banks.

agencies.name: Office of the Federal Register        (OFR)

agencies.description: The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) promotes the health, well-being, and stability of refugees, unaccompanied children, and other eligible individuals and families through culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based services.

agencies.name: Rehabilitation Services Administration        (RSA)
agencies.description: The Rehabilitation Services Administration (RSA) oversees grant programs that help individuals with physical or mental disabilities obtain employment and live more independently.

agencies.name: Safety and Environmental Enforcement, Bureau of        (BSEE)
agencies.description: The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) provides oversight and enforcement to promote safety, protect the environment, and conserve offshore resources.

agencies.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Office of Servicemember Affairs (OSA) addresses consumer financial challenges affecting military members, veterans, and their families.

agencies.name: Small Business Administration        (SBA)
agencies.description: The Small Business Administration (SBA) helps Americans start, build and grow businesses. Through an extensive network of field offices and partnerships, the Small Business Administration assists and protects the interests of small business concerns.

agencies.description:
The Social Security Administration (SSA) has two main functions. One is to assign Social Security numbers. The other is to run the Social Security retirement, survivors, and disability insurance programs. 

A third function is to run the Supplemental Security Income program, for people who are 65 or older, blind, or with a disability.

agencies.name: Social Security Advisory Board        (SSAB)
agencies.description: The Social Security Advisory Board (SSAB) advises the president, congress and the commissioner of Social Security on Social Security and Supplemental Security Income policy.

agencies.name: Southeastern Power Administration
agencies.description: The Southeastern Power Administration markets hydroelectric power generated by federal reservoirs to public entities in the southeastern United States.

agencies.name: Southern Command        (SOUTHCOM)
