agencies.name: Southwestern Power Administration
agencies.description: The Southwestern Power Administration markets hydroelectric power generated by federal dams to public entities in several states in the South and Southwest.

agencies.name: Space Command
agencies.description: The U.S. Space Command supports U.S. interests in space.

agencies.name: Special Counsel, Office of        (OSC)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Counsel (OSC) is an investigative and prosecutorial office that works to end government and political corruption, and to protect government employees and whistleblowers.

agencies.name: Special Education and Rehabilitative Services, Office of        (OSERS)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) provides a wide array of supports to parents, students, school districts, and states in three main areas: special education, vocational rehabilitation, and research.

agencies.name: State Justice Institute        (SJI)
agencies.description: The State Justice Institute (SJI) is a grant-making organization dedicated to improving the quality of justice in all state courts. It also works to facilitate better coordination between state and federal courts.

agencies.name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration        (SAMHSA)
agencies.description: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) works to improve substance abuse and mental health treatment services to those who are most in need of them.

agencies.name: Surface Mining, Reclamation and Enforcement, Office of        (OSMRE)
agencies.description: The Office of Surface Mining, Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) protects populations and the environment during surface coal mining operations. The Office also works to clean and put to good use abandoned mine sites. These missions are accomplished primarily through regulation and oversight of state programs.

agencies.name: Trade Representative
agencies.description: The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) negotiates with foreign governments to craft trade agreements and resolve disputes.

agencies.name: Trade and Development Agency        (USTDA)
agencies.description: The United States Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) links U.S. businesses to export opportunities by funding project planning activities, pilot projects, and reverse trade missions.

agencies.name: Transportation Security Administration        (TSA)
agencies.description: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) protects the nation's transportation systems to ensure freedom of movement for people and commerce.

agencies.name: Treasury Department
agencies.description: The Department of the Treasury manages federal finances by collecting taxes and paying bills and by managing currency, government accounts and public debt. The Department of the Treasury also enforces finance and tax laws.

agencies.name: Trustee Program
agencies.description: The U.S. Trustee Program protects the integrity of the Federal bankruptcy system. The Program monitors the conduct of bankruptcy parties and private estate trustees. It also identifies and helps investigate bankruptcy fraud and abuse.

agencies.name: U.S. AbilityOne Commission
agencies.description: The AbilityOne Commission creates job opportunities for people who are blind or have other significant disabilities in the manufacture and delivery of products and services to the Federal Government.

agencies.name: U.S. Access Board
agencies.description: The Access Board is an independent federal agency devoted to accessibility for people with disabilities. The Board develops and maintains design criteria for the built environment, transit vehicles, telecommunications equipment, and for electronic and information technology.

agencies.name: U.S. Agency for Global Media
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media, formerly known as the Broadcasting Board of Governors, broadcasts news and information about the United States and the world to audiences abroad.

agencies.name: U.S. Agency for International Development        (USAID)
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) is the principal U.S. agency to extend assistance to countries recovering from disaster, trying to escape poverty, and engaging in democratic reforms.

agencies.name: U.S. Air Force Reserve Command
agencies.description: The Air Force Reserve Command performs missions and supports Air Force operations.

agencies.name: U.S. Arctic Research Commission        (USARC)
agencies.description: The U.S. Arctic Research Commission (USARC) develops and recommends a national Arctic research policy.

agencies.name: U.S. Botanic Garden
agencies.description: The Botanic Garden is a living plant museum that educates visitors about the importance of plants to the well-being of humans, and to Earth’s fragile ecosystems.

agencies.name: U.S. Capitol Police
agencies.description: U.S. Capitol Police Officers work to protect life and property, investigate criminal acts, and enforce traffic regulations on U.S. Capitol Grounds. Officers are also responsible for protecting members, officers of Congress, and their families.

agencies.name: U.S. Chemical Safety Board        (CSB)
agencies.description: The Chemical Safety Board (CSB) investigates industrial chemical accidents.

agencies.name: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services        (USCIS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is responsible for processing immigration and naturalization applications and establishing policies regarding immigration services.

agencies.name: U.S. Commission of Fine Arts
agencies.description: The U. S. Commission of Fine Arts advises the government on matters pertaining to the arts, and to guide the architectural development of Washington.

agencies.name: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom        (USCIRF)
agencies.description: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) reviews the facts and circumstances of violations of religious freedom internationally and to make policy recommendations to the President, the Secretary of State and Congress.

agencies.name: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission        (CFTC)
agencies.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) protects the public from fraud, manipulation, and abusive practices related to the sale of commodity and financial futures and options, and to fosters open, competitive, and financially sound futures and option markets. They investigate and prosecute commodities fraud, including foreign currency schemes, energy manipulation and hedge fund fraud, and works with other federal and state agencies to bring criminal and other actions.

agencies.name: U.S. Courts of Appeal
agencies.description: The U.S. Courts of Appeal hear appeals from lower courts of both civil and criminal trials, but do not investigate the facts of a case. Rather, the Appeals Courts investigate whether or not the law has been fairly and correctly applied by the lower courts.

agencies.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection        (CBP)
agencies.description: Customs and Border Protection (CBP) prevents people from entering the country illegally or bringing anything harmful or illegal into the United States.

agencies.name: U.S. Cyber Command
agencies.description: The U.S. Cyber Command coordinates cyberspace operations to defend U.S. interests.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture        (USDA)
agencies.description: The Department of Agriculture (USDA) provides leadership on food, agriculture, natural resources, and related issues.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Commerce        (DOC)
agencies.description: The Department of Commerce (DOC) works with businesses, universities, communities, and the Nation’s workers to promote job creation, economic growth, sustainable development, and improved standards of living for Americans.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Education        (ED)
agencies.description: The Department of Education (ED) fosters educational excellence, and to ensures equal access to educational opportunity for all.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Energy        (DOE)
agencies.description: The Department of Energy (DOE) manages the United States' nuclear infrastructure and administers the country's energy policy. The Department of Energy also funds scientific research in the field.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Homeland Security        (DHS)
agencies.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) works to improve the security of the United States. The Department's work includes customs, border, and immigration enforcement, emergency response to natural and manmade disasters, antiterrorism work, and cybersecurity.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development        (HUD)
agencies.description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) administers programs that provide housing and community development assistance. The Department also works to ensure fair and equal housing opportunity for all.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Justice        (DOJ)
agencies.description: The Department of Justice (DOJ) enforces federal laws, seeks just punishment for the guilty, and ensures the fair and impartial administration of justice.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Labor        (DOL)
agencies.description: The Department of Labor (DOL) administers federal labor laws to guarantee workers' rights to fair, safe, and healthy working conditions, including minimum hourly wage and overtime pay, protection against employment discrimination, and unemployment insurance.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs        (VA)
agencies.description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) runs programs benefiting veterans and members of their families. agencies.name: U.S. Department of the Interior        (DOI)
agencies.description: The Department of the Interior (DOI) manages public lands and minerals, national parks, and wildlife refuges and upholds Federal trust responsibilities to Indian tribes and Native Alaskans. Additionally, Interior is responsible for endangered species conservation and other environmental conservation efforts.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury
agencies.description: The Department of the Treasury manages federal finances by collecting taxes and paying bills and by managing currency, government accounts and public debt. The Department of the Treasury also enforces finance and tax laws.

agencies.name: U.S. Election Assistance Commission        (EAC)
agencies.description: The Election Assistance Commission (EAC) supports state and local election officials in their efforts to ensure accessible, accurate. and secure elections. EAC develops guidance to meet the Help America Vote Act requirements, adopts voluntary voting system guidelines, and serves as a national clearinghouse of information on election administration. EAC also accredits testing laboratories and certifies voting systems, as well as audits the use of Help America Vote Act funds.

agencies.name: U.S. Fleet Forces Command        (USFFC)
agencies.description: U.S. Fleet Forces Command (USFFC) organizes, staffs, trains, maintains, and equips Navy forces, and develops fleet readiness.

agencies.name: U.S. House of Representatives

agencies.name: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement        (ICE)

agencies.description: The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM) is responsible for defending and promoting U.S. interests in the Pacific and Asia.
